                          Getting started

                          How Wealth OS works

                          What each page shows
                          • Home: your total wealth, your next step and a summary of everything else.
                          • Wealth: every account and holding, and the Portfolio Lab. Update balances lives here.
                          • Goals: each goal, what it needs a month and the road to your headline goal.
                          • Forecast: where today's money and habits lead, with your own what-ifs.
                          • Cashflow: how your monthly money turns into wealth. Update this month lives here.
                          • Settings: the details behind all of it.

                          Guides and articles

                          From the website. Opens in a new tab.

                          Questions people ask

                          Where do my figures come from?

                          From what you and your coach enter: your accounts, balances, income and spending. US-listed shares are priced automatically; everything else is the value you enter from your statements.

                          What should I update each month?

                          Your balances (Update balances on Wealth) and how the month went (Update this month on Cashflow). It takes a few minutes and keeps every projection worth trusting.

                          Is any of this financial advice?

                          No. Wealth OS shows the mechanics of your money so you can make your own decisions. Projections are illustrative, not predictions or recommendations.

                          The Everyday Investor provides financial coaching and education. We do not give regulated financial advice, and nothing in Wealth OS is a personal recommendation. If you need advice, we can point you to a regulated adviser.

                          The Everyday Investor

                          Let's start with the basics

                          Nothing here is regulated financial advice — it just helps your dashboard speak to you directly.

                          Your partner

                          Enter your own individual accounts and income in this onboarding — not combined household figures. Once your partner also has a TEI profile, your adviser can link the two into a household, and shared costs (rent, bills, anything you both pay for) can then be tagged as joint so they're counted once at the household level, not duplicated or missed on either dashboard.

                          Money in, money out

                          Rough numbers are fine for now — detailed budgeting comes later. This is what your dashboard and financial-freedom target are built from.

                          Income

                          Take-home pay (after tax and any salary sacrifice) — not gross salary.

                          Fixed expenses

                          Mortgage/rent, utilities, insurance — the costs that don't change month to month.

                          Variable expenses

                          Lifestyle spending, general spending, anything else that moves around.

                          Emergency fund

                          A cash buffer before anything else gets invested. Most people aim for 3–6 months of essential costs. Set your target here — once you've added a cash account (next), link it in Cashflow settings so "currently have" always matches its real balance.
                          Your monthly saving & investing rate is calculated automatically from the accounts you add next — no need to enter it separately.

                          What do you own and owe?

                          Approximate figures are fine — this becomes your net worth picture.

                          Property

                          Do you own property?

                          Other assets

                          Anything you own that isn't held in an investment account — vehicles, collectibles, business interests, and so on. Cash, ISAs, GIAs and pensions are captured as accounts on the next step.

                          Liabilities

                          Mortgage, loans, credit — what you owe.

                          Your investment accounts

                          Do you have any investment accounts — ISA, pension, GIA, LISA?

                          What's inside those accounts?

                          Entirely optional — skip this if you're not sure yet or don't have it to hand. You (or your adviser) can add it anytime.

                          What are you working towards?

                          A house deposit, financial independence, a tax-efficiency action — whatever it is. Add one or a few.
                          Linked account(s)

                          Any documents to keep handy?

                          Statements, reports, anything worth having on file. Entirely optional — skip if you don't have anything to hand.

                              Key opportunities

                                Insights

                                Generated observations pulled from across the Client Foundation — only shown where there's something worth flagging.

                                What's changed

                                Showing everything on file — nothing has been marked reviewed yet.

                                Personal

                                Investor stage

                                Wealth OS suggests a stage automatically from portfolio size, holdings and accounts. Override it here if needed.

                                Accounts

                                ISA, GIA, pension, LISA, Cash ISA, current/deposit or other. Current value seeds this month's balance automatically — adjust it below for later months.
                                More options
                                Total contributions to date is calculated from monthly deposits plus any contributions before tracking started. Cash balance = uninvested cash, added on top of holdings so totals reconcile. Interest rate (Cash ISA/Deposit only) accrues monthly — Fixed + Maturity date stops it at term. Joint account appears once linked to a household; stays edited here, read-only elsewhere. Pension splits personal/salary-sacrifice.

                                Recurring contribution —

                                Applied automatically on the day each month: each fund's value and cost basis rise by its share. Statement values entered later replace the value. No back-dating — a change applies from the next run date.
                                Enter from the client's fact find. Use gross salary.
                                Funds
                                Fill in the figures to see the monthly breakdown.

                                Contribution history

                                Rule versions

                                Pension contribution flags — all clients

                                Income changed on a client with a salary-derived rule. The annual uplift is held until each is resolved.

                                Log a month's balances

                                Building this up month by month is what powers Progress and the projections. Pick any month — past or present — to add or correct it.

                                Holdings

                                What sits inside each account. For bulk entry use CSV / Spreadsheet Import instead. Holdings set to Auto (US) are repriced automatically each weekday at 15:00, 17:00, 19:00 and 21:15 UK time — everything else keeps the value entered by hand.

                                Log a month's holdings

                                Same monthly pattern as account balances, extended to individual holdings. Pick any month — past or present — to add or correct it.

                                Dividend history

                                Actual dividend income received, by year. Powers the historical chart and growth rate on Portfolio.

                                Dividend holdings

                                Wealth — Property & Other Assets

                                Property is stored as an asset (type: property). Cash, ISAs, GIAs and pensions belong in Accounts, not here.

                                Cashflow — Income

                                Take-home pay (after tax and any salary sacrifice) — not gross salary.

                                Cashflow — Expenses

                                Fixed
                                Variable
                                One-off costs — irregular items (e.g. car repair, annual insurance renewal) included in this month's plan only while enabled. Untick to keep the record without counting it.

                                Cashflow — Saving, Emergency Fund & Preferences

                                Monthly savings and investing are calculated from account contribution fields, not typed here — see Accounts. Personal pension contributions count as investing; employer/salary sacrifice counts as neither, since it never touches take-home pay.

                                Documents & meeting notes

                                Holdings CSV import

                                Broker export with Ticker, Units, Average price (or Book cost/Value) columns. Replaces that account's holdings list.

                                Upload statements, screenshots or PDFs

                                There is no automated OCR or PDF extraction in this build — no backend to run it against. Files queue here for manual review: open the file, key the figures into Manual Entry, then mark it approved. This keeps the audit trail honest rather than pretending to extract data that was never actually read.

                                Review queue

                                Review & export

                                Every save on this page already goes straight to this client's account. Exporting just downloads a snapshot client.json for your own records or to hand to a colleague.
